perf.summary: Trial division checks every p including all even p>2 and recomputes p*p each iteration; handle 2 separately then step odd, and compare p against a running sqrt bound to avoid the multiply.
perf.currentCost: Loop tests p=2,3,4,5,... with two divisions (n%p and the while) per p and a 64-bit multiply p*p in the condition every iteration; even p>2 can never divide a reduced n yet still cost a modulo.
perf.proposedChange: Peel p=2: if((n&1)==0){result*=2; do n>>=1; while((n&1)==0);} then loop p=3; p*p<=n; p+=2. Optionally hoist the bound: since n only shrinks, the p*p<=n test stays but p+=2 halves iteration count. Use (n&1)==0 instead of n%2.
perf.rationale: Skipping even candidates halves the trial-division iterations; the &1 / >>1 for the factor-2 phase replaces modulo/division with mask/shift. n only decreases so the p*p bound shrinks favorably.
perf.risk: Must extract factor 2 before the odd loop or 2's contribution is lost — straightforward. p*p can overflow only for n beyond ~9.2e18 (long max) where p approaches 3e9; within long-valid n the bound p*p<=n keeps p below sqrt(n) so no overflow. (n&1) is exact for all n since n>=1 here (n could be negative? Run assumes n>=1 per unchecked convention).
